item.title: fix(core): don't turn truncated streamed tool-call arguments into a tool call
item.body:
Fixes #11469

**Problem.** When a stream ends partway through a tool call's arguments, `collapseToolCallChunks` repairs the partial JSON with `parsePartialJson`. The aggregated message then has a complete-looking entry in `tool_calls` and nothing in `invalid_tool_calls`, so agents built on `invoke()` (e.g. `createReactAgent`) run the tool with half its input. This happens on `finish_reason: "length"`, and also when the stream simply ends (no finish reason, no `[DONE]`), which is what a dropped connection or proxy looks like.

**Change.**
- `collapseToolCallChunks(chunks, { final: true })` parses with `JSON.parse`, the rule the non-streaming path (`parseToolCall`) already applies. The default is unchanged.
- `BaseChatModel` applies it once a stream has ended, in both places a streamed message is assembled: its own aggregation (streaming callbacks, e.g. LangGraph's `messages` mode) and the result of `_generate` for providers that stream inside it (e.g. `ChatOpenAI` with `streaming: true`).
- Chunks yielded while streaming keep the partial parse, so progressive rendering is unchanged.

It does not key on the finish reason, so it also covers the dropped-stream case, which #11494 (closed) could not.

**Relation to #11471.** #11471 addresses the same issue and has been open since August. Two differences worth checking against it, both in `libs/langchain-core/src/messages/utils.ts`:

1. #11471 passes a `truncated` flag gated on `response_metadata.finish_reason === "length"`. A stream that simply ends (no finish reason, no `[DONE]`) never sets it, so that path still produces a repaired call.
2. Its strict check runs before the `if (usesRawInputArgs && id)` branch, so `JSON.parse(argsStr)` also applies to raw-input/custom tools whose arguments are deliberately not JSON. That is the question drew-chen left on #11471 and it is still open. Here the strict parse happens inside the existing `try`, which is reached only after that branch has already `continue`d, so raw-input tools are untouched.

If you would rather land #11471, I am glad to rebase this onto it or carry the dropped-stream and raw-input cases over there instead — either way the fix should not depend on the finish reason.

**Tests.** `truncated_tool_calls.test.ts`: 7 tests, 3 fail before the change. They cover both aggregation paths, a complete call (with an escaped newline) still producing a tool call, mid-stream chunks staying lenient, and empty args still meaning `{}`. Full `@langchain/core` unit suite: 1556 passed, 1 skipped; the 5 failures (`count_tokens`, the tracer snapshot) time out the same way without this change, because they need network access. oxlint, oxfmt and tsc are clean.

**End to end**, `ChatOpenAI({ streaming: true }).invoke()` against a fake endpoint (tool calls / invalid tool calls):

| stream | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cut mid-arguments, `finish_reason: "length"` | 1 / 0 | 0 / 1 |
| cut mid-arguments, stream just ends | 1 / 0 | 0 / 1 |
| complete call | 1 / 0 | 1 / 0 |

**Not in scope.** Code that iterates `.stream()` and concatenates the chunks itself still gets the repaired call, because the chunks carry no end-of-stream marker. Python's core marks the final chunk with `chunk_position="last"`; a similar marker would be a follow-up, and I'm happy to do it if you want that direction.

The Python side is tracked in langchain-ai/langchain#41285. Agent-level reproduction across frameworks: https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-cutoff-bench

timeline.message:
fix(core): don't turn truncated streamed tool-call arguments into a tool call

Once a stream has ended, re-derive tool calls from tool_call_chunks with
JSON.parse, the rule the non-streaming path already applies. A call whose
arguments were cut off (output limit or a stream that just ends) lands in
invalid_tool_calls with the raw string instead of being repaired into a
complete-looking call. Covers aggregation in BaseChatModel and providers
that stream inside _generate. Chunks seen while streaming keep the
partial parse.

Fixes #11469

issue.title: Truncated streamed tool arguments are repaired into valid-looking tool_calls
core: truncated tool-call arguments are parsed leniently after the stream ends, producing a valid-looking tool call

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Related to a bug, vulnerability, unexpected error with an existing feature

issue.body:
### Submission checklist

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Package (Required)

- [ ] langchain
- [ ] langchain-openai
- [ ] langchain-anthropic
- [ ] langchain-classic
- [x] langchain-core
- [ ] langchain-model-profiles
- [ ] langchain-tests
- [ ] langchain-text-splitters
- [ ] langchain-chroma
- [ ] langchain-deepseek
- [ ] langchain-exa
- [ ] langchain-fireworks
- [ ] langchain-groq
- [ ] langchain-huggingface
- [ ] langchain-mistralai
- [ ] langchain-nomic
- [ ] langchain-ollama
- [ ] langchain-openrouter
- [ ] langchain-perplexity
- [ ] langchain-qdrant
- [ ] langchain-typesafe
- [ ] langchain-xai
- [ ] Other / not sure / general

### Related Issues / PRs

- #39275: same report, auto-closed for submission format, not reviewed on the merits.
- #38682 and #35743 (empty-args handling during streaming): adjacent but different.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import generate_from_stream
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessageChunk
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGenerationChunk

chunks = [
    ChatGenerationChunk(message=AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=[
        {"name": "edit_document", "args": "", "id": "call_1", "index": 0, "type": "tool_call_chunk"}])),
    ChatGenerationChunk(message=AIMessageChunk(content="", tool_call_chunks=[
        {"name": None, "args": '{"operation": "replace", "blocks": [{"type": "hea',
         "id": None, "index": 0, "type": "tool_call_chunk"}])),
]
msg = generate_from_stream(iter(chunks)).generations[0].message
print(msg.tool_calls)
# [{'name': 'edit_document', 'args': {'operation': 'replace', 'blocks': [{'type': 'hea'}]}, ...}]
print(msg.invalid_tool_calls)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

No error or stack trace. The bug is silent: a tool call whose arguments were cut off by the end of the stream comes out as a valid-looking tool call.

Running the reproduction above prints:

```python
  msg.tool_calls
  [{'name': 'edit_document', 'args': {'operation': 'replace', 'blocks': [{'type': 'hea'}]}, 'id': 'call_1', 'type': 'tool_call'}]

  msg.invalid_tool_calls
  []
```
Expected: the truncated arguments land in invalid_tool_calls (raw string preserved) and tool_calls is empty.

### Description

`AIMessageChunk.init_tool_calls` parses every tool-call chunk's `args` with `parse_partial_json`. That's right while a stream is in flight. But it's also used for the final aggregated message: both the `chunk_position="last"` chunk and the message that `generate_from_stream` builds for `invoke()` / `ainvoke()` with `streaming=True`.

If a stream ends partway through a tool call's arguments, partial parsing closes the open strings and brackets and returns a well-formed dict:
- the call lands in `tool_calls`;
- `invalid_tool_calls` stays empty;
- the tool runs with half of its input.

Streams end early more often than you'd think:
- a provider or proxy closes the connection;
- a gateway that reports a dropped upstream with `finish_reason: "stop"` (we saw this with an LLM proxy);
- a timeout in an intermediary.

Our concrete case: half of a document-edit payload was applied as a complete edit.

### System Info

System Information
------------------
> OS:  Darwin
> OS Version:  Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0: Tue Aug 11 21:06:40 PDT 2026; root:xnu-13432.1.9~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050
> Python Version:  3.11.15 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:46:51) [Clang 22.1.3 ]

Package Information
-------------------
> langchain_core: 1.6.12
> langsmith: 0.14.9
> langchain_protocol: 0.0.18
> langchain_tests: 1.1.9

### Social handles (optional)

_No response_

+---
+"@langchain/core": patch
+---
+
+fix(core): once a stream has ended, tool-call arguments must be complete JSON; a call cut off mid-arguments now lands in `invalid_tool_calls` instead of running with half its input
